caption:
For years, Canadian athletes Marissa Papaconstantinou, Monica Wright Rogers and Sarah Mitton have pushed their bodies to the limit—on the track, the court and the field. Yet the pressures they face aren’t just about performance. “People don’t see, when you’re out there and you’re racing, how much discomfort you can be in,” says Papaconstantinou, who got her period on the final day of the 2025 World Para Athletics Championships. “It speaks to the strength and perseverance that female athletes have at this level.”

Ahead of International Women’s Day, these stars spoke to The Kit about the thorniest aspects of living and competing in a woman’s body, from menstruation to motherhood to simultaneously hearing your body is too big and too small.

caption:
Friendly reminder that all body’s are different!! 🫶🏼

I train 5 days a week, lift 3 days with a Pilates workout on an off day. I eat high levels of protein for recovery, I’m very limited on sugars, I take supplements that are necessary for health and performance, I don’t drink alcohol, I sleep 9-10 hours a night, and I drink 3 litres of water a day. This is just my body, and yes at different times of the year I lean out, I lower BFP that happens naturally with training but it’s never to the degree I “aesthetically” used to wish it would. When you’re doing all the right things and you’re still not seeing “lean” results don’t be so hard on yourself cause all bodies are different. I train my body for performance and I give myself what I need to be strong and fast (at least I try most of the time). Here’s your sign to hit goals to be the most healthy version of yourself, and forget fitting into the narrative/mould of what society has continually pushed on us. 

#running #trackandfield #travel #bodypositive #fitness #wellbeing #training #weightlifting #womeninspiringwomen #bekind

This International Women’s Day join us in honouring Marissa’s inspiring journey—proof that with the right care, community, and an unwavering spirit, there’s no limit to what women can achieve!

caption:
If you were to ask me how I felt about my performance and experience at the Paralympics, I’d say that I under performed, I didn’t hit the times I wanted, and I missed the podium. But if you asked me on a deeper level…

I’d say I’m really proud of the way I handled this season, because it was hard. Fighting through setbacks, injury, and the pressure of expectation going into my 3rd Paralympic Games.

I’d say I fought my hardest getting to those starting lines feeling the way I did because I was a lot sicker than I was willing to admit. I’m never one to make excuses for myself so regardless of how it felt I wanted to fight my way to each finish line.

I’d say how grateful I was to have 25 of my family and friends cheering me on in the stands, I have never felt more loved and supported in my life. 

I’d say how proud I was of my teammates and the entirety of the Paralympic movement. Every single athlete at this Paralympic Games through triumph and heartbreak inspired a generation of people with disabilities to believe they can achieve anything and set remarkable goals in pursuit of excellence. 

I’d say that racing in front of a crowd of 80,000 people in Stade de France and millions more tuning in around the world will be an experience I will never forget. PEOPLE CARE ABOUT THE PARALYMPICS.

I’d say that I’m extremely appreciative and thankful for the support that’s been in my corner to get me here. My coach @bobwestman for instilling belief in every single thing I do day in and day out. My wonderful parents that have never taken no for an answer and have created every opportunity possible. My sister Kristin for always lifting me up, and being my source of inspiration on the days I lack motivation. My partner Justyn for being my rock and always having the right thing to say through tough times. 

I’d say that I can gain this as experience and I’m so fortunate to do what I love every day. I choose to cherish these moments because winning, losing and pressure is all a privilege. 

Thank you to all of you for the endless support. I can’t wait for more growth and faster races in the future. Lots of love, 

Canada’s Blade Runner ❤️🤍

📸 @seeyouatgate3

caption:
How do you manage bumps in the road? I’ve been dealing with a back injury for the past few weeks and it’s definitely been new territory for me, not like your typical hamstring strain. It gets better, then it gets worse and I’ve been having trouble understanding what my body needs and wants through the process. Although it’s not a place I want to be in, I’m taking it as an opportunity to grow my horizons, learn more about my body and correct my weaknesses. How do I do that? 

1) Creating a solid rehab plan with my coach and team around me 

2) Mentally prepare for bumps in the plan, you might need to go to plan b or c or even d on that day

3) Follow through with the plan while holding myself accountable everyday 

4) Communication, and being open about physical and emotional struggles

5) Taking care and being kind to myself. This involves meditation, spending time outdoors with my dog, sleeping, eating and hydrating well
